answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a forge-built registry before it can vote or claim rewards. A rate limit then caps each verified account’s influence, while slashing the bond when an account is caught coordinating fraud. This does not prove a person is unique, but it makes a Sybil swarm costly: the attacker must acquire and immobilize many tokens, and risks losing them. A trellis of attestations may help link accounts, while a canyon of separate wallets alone proves nothing.
